texts.passage: Visitor notice: The public transport information guide will take place at the transport centre on Wednesday afternoon. Participants must register before joining and should arrive ten minutes early. There is no fee for school pupils.

Email: Dear Salim, we discovered an outdated departure time in our original notice. We checked the official route timetable and corrected the information. Please use the new version when contacting visitors and avoid distributing the old message.
texts.statement: Salim should use the inaccurate notice.

texts.passage: Information desk: Our programme provides simple explanations for daily passengers. Visitors can ask about accessibility and practical arrangements. The organisers will answer politely and direct people to an appropriate member of staff when they need further assistance.
texts.statement: The information desk refuses to answer visitors' questions.

texts.passage: Survey report: Thirty participants answered questions after the visit. Eighteen found the revised information clearer, seven requested extra detail and five were uncertain. The team agreed to review these comments before preparing another event. Please contact the organisers for further information.

texts.passage: Coordinator's note: The transport coordinator will check the final announcement before publication. Students should record all changes, especially those affecting safety or schedules. The purpose is trustworthy information rather than collecting followers on social media.

texts.passage: Community message: The event will use reusable materials wherever practical, and participants should leave shared spaces clean. Volunteers are asked to respect local residents, follow safety advice and report any concerns to the organising teacher.
texts.statement: Volunteers should keep public spaces clean.

texts.passage: Reminder: The public transport information guide is designed for learning and will not replace official professional services. Visitors should confirm important arrangements directly with staff and ask questions whenever a detail in the printed information seems unclear.

wrt1.title: Writing 1: Evaluative essay
wrt1.prompt: Write an evaluative essay of at least 100 words discussing the benefits and difficulties of travel and transport for local communities. Explain both sides and give your justified opinion.

wrt2.title: Writing 2: Narrative
wrt2.prompt: Write a narrative of at least 100 words beginning: 'We arrived at the meeting point, but the information on our ticket did not match the official notice.' Explain what happened, how the problem was solved and what you learned.

rdg2.title: Reading 2: Interactive university email
rdg2.passage:
Email 1 — From Sara to the visitor information team

Dear Team,

I am preparing a school group visit connected with travel and transport. Your website describes public transport information guide, but I would like to confirm the meeting arrangements. Several pupils are travelling from different areas, and one student needs information about accessibility. I would also appreciate advice about what to bring and how much time to allow for the activity.

An earlier message mentioned a different starting time. Could you please confirm which information is current? Our teacher has asked us to verify the details before collecting any payments or arranging transport. Thank you for helping us plan responsibly.

Best wishes,
Sara

Email 2 — From the information team

Dear Sara,

Thank you for your message. We apologise for the confusion caused by an outdated departure time. The current information is recorded in the official route timetable, and we have corrected our public notice. The transport coordinator will make sure that staff use the revised version.

The programme will begin at the announced meeting point in the transport centre. Please contact us before your visit if any pupil requires additional assistance. We can discuss suitable arrangements and give clear instructions. There is no school participation fee, although families should consider their own travel expenses.

Kind regards,
Information Team

Email 3 — From Sara

Dear Team,

Thank you for checking the details. I appreciate your clear explanation and your willingness to consider different visitors' needs. I will share only the revised information with our group and remind pupils to ask questions respectfully. After the activity, I hope we can send feedback about what we learned.

Best wishes,
Sara The organisers reminded students that reliable information matters more than a confident voice or an attractive photograph. They recorded where each statement came from and checked whether the source had changed recently. Some people needed simple explanations, so the group prepared clear words and invited further questions. The teacher encouraged everyone to discuss uncertainty honestly rather than present a guess as a fact. Different students contributed through careful research, writing, practical organisation and respectful discussion with visitors.

rdg3.title: Reading 3: First semester university narrative
rdg3.passage:
Reliable travel and transport information is important because people make real decisions based on what they read. Visitors may compare prices, travel times, accessibility and safety rules before choosing a service. An attractive advertisement cannot replace a clear explanation of the actual arrangements.

Good organisations prepare accurate public notices and revise them whenever circumstances change. The team managing public transport information guide must check dates and conditions against authoritative sources. A mistake such as an outdated departure time can inconvenience families and damage public trust. When an error is discovered, a responsible organisation should explain the correction openly.

Communication is another essential skill. Staff should listen before answering and avoid assuming that every person has the same needs. Somebody travelling with a child, an older relative or a person with limited mobility may require different practical information. Using simple language and inviting questions helps people understand the service without embarrassment.

Training and teamwork also affect the quality of a visitor's experience. Different staff members may handle bookings, safety checks and information. They need a shared, updated record so that visitors do not receive conflicting answers. A group can practise realistic conversations and review how an unexpected problem should be handled.

Costs and environmental responsibilities deserve attention too. Organisations can reduce unnecessary printing, use durable materials and encourage people to respect shared places. However, environmental claims should be supported by evidence rather than repeated simply because they sound positive. Visitors benefit when choices and limitations are explained honestly.

Students learning about travel and transport can develop these habits through small supervised projects. They should compare official information, identify missing details, prepare questions and discuss the possible effects of inaccurate claims. The aim is not to memorise one perfect response. It is to practise responsible judgement, cooperation and clear communication.

Ultimately, reliable transport information depends on reliable evidence and respect for different people. A service becomes more trustworthy when it welcomes feedback, corrects mistakes promptly and helps visitors make informed choices. The organisers reminded students that reliable information matters more than a confident voice or an attractive photograph. They recorded where each statement came from and checked whether the source had changed recently. Some people needed simple explanations, so the group prepared clear words and invited further questions. The teacher encouraged everyone to discuss uncertainty honestly rather than present a guess as a fact. Different students contributed through careful research, writing, practical organisation and respectful discussion with visitors.
